lesson_name: Why the Vikings came to Britain

photos.subject: A farm on a narrow strip of flat green land beside a Norwegian fjord, with steep rocky mountains rising straight out of the water behind it
photos.pedagogical_constraint: The steep ground and the small amount of flat farmland must both be visible in the same frame.
photos.teaching_requirement: See how little land a Viking family had to farm, so the shortage of farmland is something children look at rather than a fact they are told.
load_bearing_evidence: steep mountainside or rock coming down to the water
a narrow strip of flat green farmland at the water's edge
at least one farm building or field on that strip
water of a fjord or inlet

generation_prompt.physical_state: A small farm with two or three buildings and a couple of fields on a thin strip of flat green land between deep water and steep mountains.
generation_prompt.text_rule: no readable text, labels, logos or branding
generation_prompt.composition: One clear landscape frame showing the water, the narrow farmed strip and the mountain behind it.

photos.subject: The ruins of Lindisfarne Priory on Holy Island, Northumberland, with the sea and the shoreline visible close behind it
photos.pedagogical_constraint: The sea or the shore must be visible in the same frame as the monastery, and there must be no wall or fortification standing between them.
photos.teaching_requirement: See that a British monastery stood right beside the water with nothing defending it, which is what made it reachable and worth raiding.
load_bearing_evidence: the stone ruins of Lindisfarne Priory
the sea or the shoreline close behind or beside the ruins
open ground around the monastery with no defensive wall
photos.fallback_note: A generated image would invent a real place children can visit, and the raid of 793 that this slide teaches is tied to that island.

photos.subject: A Viking-age silver hoard from Britain on museum display: silver coins, arm-rings and a silver cup or bowl
photos.pedagogical_constraint: Real Viking-age silver objects, not jewellery from another period and not a film prop.
photos.teaching_requirement: See what the treasure in a monastery actually looked like, so that silver is a real object rather than a word.
load_bearing_evidence: silver objects from the Viking age
more than one object, so it reads as a hoard rather than a single item
objects clear enough to see their shape
photos.fallback_note: A generated hoard would be invented objects presented as real finds, and the slide still teaches without it because Lindisfarne carries the beat.

photos.subject: Wide, flat arable farmland in eastern England beside a river, with large open fields of wheat or barley running to the horizon
photos.pedagogical_constraint: The land must read as flat and open with a lot of it, so it contrasts with the narrow fjord strip children saw earlier.
photos.teaching_requirement: See how much good flat farmland Britain had, which is the reason Viking families came to stay rather than to take things home.
load_bearing_evidence: the fields continuing into the distance
a river or waterway in the scene

generation_prompt.physical_state: Flat, low-lying English farmland with large open fields of wheat or barley either side of a river, stretching to the horizon.
generation_prompt.text_rule: no readable text, labels, logos or branding
generation_prompt.composition: One wide landscape frame with a low horizon so the amount of flat land is obvious.
